 Fort Bend County District Court
 Cause No. 2025-CV-0025
 Ryan Roberts, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Ryan Roberts
Date:
September 15, 2025
Location:
Offices of Carter & Smith Injury Lawyers
Examining attorney:
Stephanie Williams, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Carlos Fox, Carter & Smith Injury Lawyers
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not put my full name in a transcript, but I understand this is a synthetic test document, so I'll just answer the
questions.
Q: Thnak you. Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a weekday afternoon. Traffic had slowed down on the main road near the shopping center in
Katy, so I was stopped behind a line of cars at a light.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: Describe the impact for me.
A: The vehicle beihnd me hit my rear bumper. It wasn't a huge crash in terms of how the cars looked afterward, but my head
snapped back and then forward against the headrest. I felt a sharp pain across my neck almost right away.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: I did, but I felt stiff and sore. My lower back started aching within an hour or so.
Q: Did you seek medical care that day?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same evening. They checked my range of motion, took some X-rays, and diagnosed a neck
and back strain.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've had physical therapy about three times a week. I also got a prescription for muscle relaxers and an anti-inflammatory, and
I've been using heat packs at home.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily routine?
A: Mostly in small ways that add up. I used to go to the gym regularly, and I've had to stop lifting. Sitting at my desk for long
stretches makes my back stiff, so I have to get up every half hour. Turning my head to check my blind spot when I drive is
uncomfortable, and I've asked my partner to handle the grocery runs because carrying bags aggravates my lower back.
Q: Have you missed any work?
A: I missed a few days early on and then came back on a modified schedule. I'm now able to do my job, but I take more breaks
than I used to.
Q: Before this collision, did you have any prior problems with your neck or back?
A: I had occasional tightness from long days at a computer, but nothing that required treatment or stopped me from doing things I
wanted to do.
Q: Do you currently have any restrictions from your doctor?
A: Yes. I've been told to avoid heavy lifting and repetitive twisting until my physical therapist clears me.
</page>
